```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

**Work:** Find a data set to which you can fit a multiple linear regression and interpret your results.

# 1. Functions

Each step of the analysis is a small function so it can be tested and debugged separately.

```{r functions}
# ---------- 1. Load data ----------
load_data <- function() {
  df <- datasets::mtcars
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(df), nrow(df) > 0)
  df
}

# ---------- 2. Fit model ----------
fit_model <- function(data, response = "mpg", predictors = c("wt", "hp")) {
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(data),
            is.character(response), length(response) == 1,
            is.character(predictors), length(predictors) >= 2)

  missing_cols <- setdiff(c(response, predictors), names(data))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("Column(s) not found in data: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  f <- as.formula(paste(response, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")))
  lm(f, data = data)
}

# ---------- 3. Diagnostic plots ----------
# file = NULL draws on the current device (used when knitting);
# file = "name.png" also saves a large, high-resolution image.
plot_diagnostics <- function(model, file = NULL) {
  stopifnot(inherits(model, "lm"))

  idx   <- which.max(abs(rstandard(model)))      # most extreme point
  name  <- names(rstandard(model))[idx]
  qq    <- qqnorm(rstandard(model), plot.it = FALSE)
  style <- list(pch = 19, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.4, id.n = 0)

  # Label placed ABOVE the point so it does not collide with the dots
  add_label <- function(x, y) {
    text(x, y, labels = name, pos = 3, offset = 0.9,
         cex = 1, font = 2, xpd = TRUE)
  }

  draw_all <- function() {
    do.call(plot, c(list(model, which = 1), style))
    add_label(fitted(model)[idx], resid(model)[idx])

    do.call(plot, c(list(model, which = 2), style))
    add_label(qq$x[idx], qq$y[idx])

    do.call(plot, c(list(model, which = 3), style))
    add_label(fitted(model)[idx], sqrt(abs(rstandard(model)))[idx])

    do.call(plot, c(list(model, which = 5), style))
  }

  if (!is.null(file)) {
    png(file, width = 2400, height = 2000, res = 250)
    op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
    draw_all()
    par(op)
    dev.off()
  } else {
    op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
    draw_all()
    par(op)
  }

  invisible(file)
}

# ---------- 4. Assumption tests ----------
run_tests <- function(model) {
  stopifnot(inherits(model, "lm"))

  if (!requireNamespace("car", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Package 'car' is needed. Install it with install.packages('car').")
  }

  list(
    vif     = car::vif(model),
    shapiro = shapiro.test(residuals(model))
  )
}
```

# 2. Data exploration

```{r explore}
mtcars_df <- load_data()
head(mtcars_df)
str(mtcars_df)
summary(mtcars_df[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
cor(mtcars_df[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
```

```{r pairs, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
pairs(mtcars_df[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")],
      pch = 19, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.3, cex.labels = 2)
```

# 3. Fit the multiple linear regression

```{r model}
model <- fit_model(mtcars_df)
summary(model)
confint(model)
```

# 4. Check the assumptions

## 4.1 Diagnostic plots

```{r diagnostics, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
plot_diagnostics(model)
```

To also save a high-resolution copy as an image file, run:

```{r save-diagnostics, eval=FALSE}
plot_diagnostics(model, file = "diagnostics.png")
```

## 4.2 Multicollinearity and normality

```{r tests}
tests <- run_tests(model)
tests
```

# 5. Interpretation

Replace the text below with your own interpretation after checking the output above.

- **Intercept:** predicted mpg when weight and horsepower are both 0 (not meaningful in practice).
- **wt:** holding horsepower constant, each additional 1,000 lbs is associated with a drop in mpg of about the estimated coefficient.
- **hp:** holding weight constant, each additional horsepower is associated with a small drop in mpg.
- **R² / adjusted R²:** the share of variation in mpg explained by the model.
- **F-test:** whether the model as a whole predicts mpg better than no predictors.
- **Assumptions:** discuss any curvature in Residuals vs Fitted, the Q-Q plot, the VIF values, the Shapiro-Wilk p-value, and influential cars.
- **Caveats:** only 32 cars from 1974, and the results show association, not causation.

# 6. Debugging the functions

## 6.1 Automated test of all functions

Runs each function with good and bad inputs and reports PASS, FAIL, or WARN. The bad-input rows **should** say FAIL with a clear message, which shows the validation works.

```{r test-all}
test_all <- function() {
  results <- list()

  check <- function(label, expr) {
    out <- tryCatch({ force(expr); "PASS" },
                    error   = function(e) paste("FAIL:", conditionMessage(e)),
                    warning = function(w) paste("WARN:", conditionMessage(w)))
    results[[label]] <<- out
  }

  d <- load_data()
  m <- fit_model(d)

  # Normal use
  check("load_data()",                 load_data())
  check("fit_model() good input",      fit_model(d))
  check("plot_diagnostics() good",     plot_diagnostics(m, tempfile(fileext = ".png")))
  check("run_tests() good",            run_tests(m))

  # Deliberately bad input
  check("fit_model() bad column",      fit_model(d, predictors = c("weight", "hp")))
  check("fit_model() one predictor",   fit_model(d, predictors = "wt"))
  check("fit_model() not a data.frame", fit_model(as.matrix(d)))
  check("plot_diagnostics() not lm",   plot_diagnostics("not a model"))
  check("run_tests() not lm",          run_tests(42))

  data.frame(test = names(results), result = unlist(results), row.names = NULL)
}

test_all()
```

## 6.2 Catch an error and see where it came from

`traceback()` only works interactively, so inside a knitted document we catch the error and print the call that caused it.

```{r catch-error}
tryCatch(
  fit_model(mtcars_df, predictors = c("weight", "hp")),
  error = function(e) {
    cat("Error message:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    cat("Raised in call:", deparse(conditionCall(e)), "\n")
  }
)
```

## 6.3 Switch debugging on and off for every function

```{r debug-flags}
fns <- c("load_data", "fit_model", "plot_diagnostics", "run_tests")

invisible(lapply(fns, debug))            # turn debugging ON
sapply(fns, isdebugged)                  # confirm
invisible(lapply(fns, undebug))          # turn debugging OFF
sapply(fns, isdebugged)                  # confirm it is off
```

## 6.4 Watch a function without editing it

```{r trace-demo}
trace("fit_model",
      quote(cat("Fitting with predictors:", predictors, "\n")),
      print = FALSE)
invisible(fit_model(mtcars_df))
untrace("fit_model")
```

## 6.5 Interactive debugging (run these in the R console, not when knitting)

These open the `Browse[2]>` prompt, which needs a live R session, so the chunks are set to `eval=FALSE`.

```{r interactive-debug, eval=FALSE}
debugonce(load_data);        load_data()
debugonce(fit_model);        m <- fit_model(mtcars)
debugonce(plot_diagnostics); plot_diagnostics(m)
debugonce(run_tests);        run_tests(m)
```

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `n` or Enter | run the next line |
| `s` | step into a function call |
| `c` | continue to the end of the function |
| `Q` | quit the debugger |
| `ls()` | list local variables |
| `print(x)` | inspect a variable |

Pause at an exact line by adding `browser()` inside a function, for example just before `lm()` in `fit_model()`. A conditional version, `if (anyNA(data)) browser()`, only stops when something is wrong.

To enter the debugger automatically on any error, and to turn it off afterwards:

```{r recover, eval=FALSE}
options(error = recover)
options(error = NULL)
```
